A right turn on a circular red signal is permitted only after a complete stop, when safe and when no sign prohibits it. A circular yellow signal means red is coming; stop unless already in the intersection or too close to stop safely. If the light turns yellow while entering the intersection, proceed with extreme caution. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. narration.text: A circular green signal permits a legal maneuver only when the intersection is clear and no traffic-control device prohibits it. Even with a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection or entering with the right of way. When turning left on a circular green light, yield to opposing vehicles going straight. A steady red arrow prohibits the indicated movement; stop before the crosswalk or stop line, or before the intersection if neither exists. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.
